title: Chapter 15. Morning Lilas in Navadvipa
html:
Gaura's remnants from Shachi; kirtana along the Ganga to the village of Gadigachha; a feast with the cowherds — Bhima and his mother Shyama; the crocodile in the pond — a son of the demigods cursed by Durvasa — delivered by kirtana; the pond Goradaha (pp. 40–45)

[p. 40]

1Whatever deeds of Gauranga come to mind at any time,
those I write down, though not in order.

2One day Mother Shachi, with great care,
held out to me the dish with the remnants of Gora's meal.

3I ate as if tasting nectar:
receiving Gauranga's prasada, my mind rejoiced.

4Shall I ever again taste that bountiful meal —
Ai's cooking: fresh unsalted greens,1

5banana-flower stew, taro greens with phulabadi,
slices of mankachu, neem with patol, and dahibadi?

6Joyful after the meal, we went with a swan's gait
together with Nitai, Gauranga and their companions;
walking along the bank of the Ganga, we came to the village of Gadigachha,
singing the names of Hari.2

7Govinda plays the mridanga, Vasu Ghosh sings the Name,
Gadadhara and Vakreshvara dance;3
at the sound of "Haribol" — joyful cries on every side:
all are intoxicated with love for Gora.

[p. 41]

8I know neither dance nor song — and still I dance with arms raised:
Gauranga, entering my body, makes me dance;
I have no sense of tune or rhythm — and still I dance, still I sing:
who knows what is in the mind of moonlike Gaura!

9Coming to the village of Gadigachha, entering the cowherds' settlement,
Gora says: "Listen, devotees!
To roam the bank of the pond — that is our outing today;
we shall lie down at the roots of the trees.

10Under this banyan the cows are grazing happily:
let us play with the cowherds."
Many cowherds came and gave yogurt, curd and butter —
and no trace of the journey's fatigue remained.

11With Nrisimhananda Pradyumna came joyfully,
and Purushottama Acharya joined them;4
at the sound of the mridanga all left their homes,
and the cry of "Hari!" rose to the sky.

12A cowherd named Bhima, a man of great generosity,
stepped forward and said: "Hear my request!

[p. 42]

13My mother is the blessed milkmaid Shyama,
daughter of a pious cowherd of Ganganagara.

14She calls Mother Shachi "mother" and always serves her:
by that kinship You are my maternal uncle.

15Uncle, uncle, come to my house with all Your people,
joyfully perform Sri Krishna-kirtana.

16Yogurt, milk — whatever mother has put by —
I will feed you all, and massage your feet as well."

17When all begged insistently,
out of love for the cowherds Gora went to the cowherd's house.

18Shyama the milkmaid, with joyful ululation,
led everyone into the cowshed.

19Shyama says: "Brother Pandita, how is mother?"
"Well, well," answers Gora, swaying in dance.

20Spreading banana leaves, Shyama serves yogurt and sweet rice;
with the devotees Nimai sits down leisurely to eat.

21Having finished the meal, He goes to the bank of that pond;
all leisurely sing the qualities of Hari.

[p. 43]

22The cowherd Ramadasa comes and reports:
"The cows will not drink the water of the pond.

23In the water of the pond roams a fearsome crocodile:
without drinking, the cows low."

24Hearing this, Gora performs Sri Nama-kirtana;
the kirtana at once drew the crocodile.

25Quickly emerging, it came to Gora's feet:
by the touch of His feet a divine form appears.

26Weeping, this son of the demigods offers praise,
tells of his misfortune and sobs.

27The son of the demigods says: "Lord! By Durvasa's curse
I wander in the form of a crocodile, and all the worlds tremble.

28In Kamyavana the best of sages lay resting;
out of mischief I cut off his matted locks.

29In anger the sage said: 'Take the form of a crocodile;
remain so for four yugas — the fruit of your deed.'

30Then I wept, entreating him;
in mercy the sage called me to him and said:

[p. 44]

31'Son of the demigods! When Sri Nandanandana
becomes in Navadvipa the treasure of Shachi's life,

32by His kirtana your curse will end:
gaining a divine body, you will go to Tripishtapa.'"5

33"Glory, glory to the son of Shachi, purifier of the fallen,
refuge of the poor, the lowly and the helpless, the Great One!

34In all fourteen worlds Your good fame resounds:
You have saved one as fallen as I.

35This Navadvipa-dhama is the essence of all abodes:
here You have become the purifier of the fallen of Kali.

36You will save the jivas of Kali by giving them the name of Hari:
You have come, Mahaprabhu! Obeisance to You.

37For four yugas I bore the form of a crocodile;
now You have saved me, Hari, purifier of the fallen.

38The name of Hari from Your lips is supremely sweet:
You have saved a multitude of moving and unmoving beings.

39Give me leave to go to Tripishtapa:
seeing my mother and father, I shall be happy in every way."

40Saying this and bowing down, the son of the demigods departs;
and then the roar of kirtana rises again.

[p. 45]

41Seeing that the day was drawing to its close, all the devotees
set out with the Lord for Mayapura.

42Whoever hears this lila of Mahaprabhu —
that great soul is freed from a brahmana's curse.

43From then on the name "Goradaha" spread:
the pond became like the Kaliya-daha.6

44Seeing this pond and touching it, people destroy their sins
and gain devotion to Krishna — so say all the Vedas.

45Look at those cowherds in the great bliss of love:
here, calling Gauranga "uncle", they carried Him on their shoulders.

46All saw the Lord's morning outing —
and in it they saw the essence of the lila of Rama and Krishna.

47There they see Govardhana, the bank of the Manasa-Ganga,
the lila of Krishna herding the cows — all exactly so.

48The cowherds understood that Nimai's deeds
are that very lila of Sri Nanda-nandana, desired by Him Himself.7

Notes

  1. Abona achut shak — the reading is unclear (cf. ch. 5, n. 2). The dishes are Bengali: mochaghanta (stewed banana flower), kachu-shak (taro greens), phulabadi (dried lentil-flour dumplings), manchaki (slices of giant taro, man-kachu), nimba-patol (neem with patol), dadhibadi (dumplings in yogurt).
  2. Gadigachha — a village on the island of Godruma in the Navadvipa-mandala (cf. Bhaktivinoda Thakura's Navadvipa-dhama-mahatmya). This whole lila (ch. 15) — the cowherds Bhima, Shyama and Ramadasa, the pond Goradaha, the deliverance of the son of the demigods — is known only from the Prema-vivarta.
  3. Govinda (Ghosh) and Vasu Ghosh — kirtaniya brothers of Navadvipa (CC Adi 10.115).
  4. According to the CC (Antya 2), Nrisimhananda is the name the Lord gave to Pradyumna Brahmachari, i.e. one person; here they are named as if two. Purushottama Acharya is Svarupa Damodara's name before sannyasa, when he lived in Navadvipa with the Lord (CC Madhya 10.103).
  5. Tripishtapa — Indra's heavenly planet, the world of the demigods.
  6. Daha — a deep pond or pool. The Kaliya-daha — the pool in the Yamuna where the serpent Kaliya lived, subdued by Krishna.
  7. Verses 45–48 express the teaching of the non-difference of Navadvipa and Vraja: the devotees see in Gadigachha Govardhana, the Manasa-Ganga and Krishna's cowherd games.
